proposals.name: County Operating Tax Levy
proposals.description:
Shall the voted allocated Montmorency County millage rate of 5.7500 mills ($5.75 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 4.8204 mills ($4.8204 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be increased by up to 0.9296 mills ($0.9296 per $1,000 of taxable value) to the 1976 original allocated rate to recover that millage reduction and be levied by Montmorency County for Eight (8) years (2026-2034 inclusive), for general operating purposes?
If approved and levied in full, this…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall the voted allocated Montmorency County millage rate of 5.7500 mills ($5.75 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 4.8204 mills ($4.8204 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be increased by up to 0.9296 mills ($0.9296 per $1,000 of taxable value) to the 1976 original allocated rate to recover that millage reduction and be levied by Montmorency County for Eight (8) years (2026-2034 inclusive), for general operating purposes?
If approved and levied in full, this Millage will raise an estimated additional $643,427 for general County operating purposes in the first calendar year of the levy based on state taxable valuation.
proposals.officialTitle: COUNTY OPERATING TAX LEVY
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 5.75 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.name: General Operations Millage Proposal
proposals.description: This proposal will authorize Albert Township to levy up to 0.5 mills to fund general township operations. This would cost you $0.50 for every $1,000 of your taxable real and personal property. The millage would be charged annually for five years, from 2026 through 2031, inclusive. The millage would raise an estimated $100,389 in the first year. Should the proposed millage be approved?
proposals.ballotLanguage: This proposal will authorize Albert Township to levy up to 0.5 mills to fund general township operations. This would cost you $0.50 for every $1,000 of your taxable real and personal property. The millage would be charged annually for five years, from 2026 through 2031, inclusive. The millage would raise an estimated $100,389 in the first year. Should the proposed millage be approved?
proposals.officialTitle: GENERAL OPERATIONS MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 0.5 mills for 5 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.

proposals.description:
This proposal will permit the intermediate school district to continue to levy special education millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 1.2872 mills ($1.2872 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Alpena-Montmorency-Alcona Educational Service District, Michigan, to provide funds for the education of students with a disability, be renewed for a period of 10 years,…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will permit the intermediate school district to continue to levy special education millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 1.2872 mills ($1.2872 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Alpena-Montmorency-Alcona Educational Service District, Michigan, to provide funds for the education of students with a disability, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2027 to 2036, inclusive; the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $3,536,404 from local property taxes authorized herein (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: ALPENA-MONTMORENCY-ALCONA EDUCATIONAL SERVICE DISTRICT SPECIAL EDUCATION MILLAGE RENEWAL PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 1.2872 mills for 10 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.
